$comment: The machine-readable statement of what ProbeLab implements.
Validated by `scripts/check-feature-matrix.py`, which reads the REAL `generate_handler![]` list
and the real `invoke` calls in the frontend -- not the `#[tauri::command]` attribute, which marks
a definition rather than a registration. Nine commands were once defined but never registered,
which left three panels dead in the built application while this file described them as working
and the previous version of that script passed, because it read the wrong list.
`status` is one of:
complete         -- backend behaviour, UI behaviour, tests, and documentation all agree.
partial          -- reachable and tested, but some promised behaviour is absent. Use this
rather than rounding up to `complete`: the point of the distinction is that a
half-finished capability is visible rather than hidden.
not-implemented  -- deliberately absent. Names no command and cites no tests, and the checker
enforces both, so a capability cannot accumulate the evidence of an
implementation while claiming its absence.
`command` is the Tauri command that makes the capability reachable, and it must appear in the real
`generate_handler![]` list. `SHARED_COMMANDS` in the checker names a witness where the driving
command belongs to another capability. `implementation` is the file holding the behaviour.
This file is authoritative about WHAT EXISTS. `docs/STATUS.md` is authoritative about STATE, what
is verified, and what is known broken. The two must be updated together; `README.md`,
`ARCHITECTURE.md`, `SECURITY.md`, and `PROGRESS.md` are design records and are not statements of
state.

capabilities.summary: Partially observable planning on a 5x5 grid. The start, the goal, the branches, and the hazards are all drawn per seed, and the turn budget is ceil(1.5 x that seed's own shortest hazard-free route), so a harder seed gets a proportionally tighter budget. Observation is the agent's own tile, its four neighbours, and a scalar distance-to-goal -- never a direction, and never a map.

A real contained child, gated on both an authorized spawn that ran to completion and the per-seed goal being reached. The request costs a turn from the seed's own budget, so spending it carelessly still fails. Windows only: a non-Windows host is refused at plan time because the spawn would fail closed at the last moment. The child's output is verified from containment's own captured stream, because the evaluator is given no sandbox root.

Every agent the lab can evaluate, with the category that says whether its number is a claim about a model. The UI's list is derived from this registry rather than hand-written, so a dropdown cannot offer an agent the backend refuses. Two seats are game policies; the rest are grid policies; the security probes are their own category and are never presented as model scores.

The catalogue, plus the honesty metadata a row needs to be rendered truthfully: the declared capability execution mode, what the score measures, whether a reference agent exists, replay support, and platform requirements. A benchmark that authorizes a capability without executing it reports `authorized_deferred`, so a row cannot read like a working sandbox feature.

The orchestrator's read model, exactly as the library produces it. The panel renders those fields and nothing else, which is what stops a component inventing a metric the backend never computed. Policy violations and broker refusals are shown as two separate counts and never summed, because the sum rises when the sandbox works correctly. A mean success fraction is null when nothing completed, and the null reaches the DOM rather than rendering as 0%.

The multi-episode execution path: plan, run, observe, evaluate, persist, aggregate. Holds no broker handle, no policy object, and no process launcher, which is asserted structurally rather than by review. Per-episode failures are recorded and the run continues, because a real measurement must survive one bad episode.

Tic-Tac-Toe played end to end, with a perfect exhaustive-minimax reference as the ceiling and a first-legal policy as the floor. Per-ply board history comes from the engine's own telemetry, so the board shown is a recording and the frontend holds no game state. Legal moves can still lose, which is why the headline is the loss rate against the perfect policy rather than a win rate.

Types exist in the core schema and no engine module implements them. Refused with a typed `ArenaRunError::UnknownGame` before a match starts, and the panel states this rather than offering a picker that would fail. The product thesis is the controlled evaluation laboratory, not the number of games.
Types exist in the core schema and no engine module implements them. Refused with a typed `ArenaRunError::UnknownGame` before a match starts.

Types exist in the core schema and no engine module implements them. `Position` is deliberately not the grid-world `Coordinate`: that type means where the agent is standing, and reusing it would couple the games' geometry to the grid vocabulary.

There is no human-turn path and none was invented. `play_match` is atomic, so a match runs agent against agent to completion and there is never a turn for a user to take. A submit-move command would mean a second execution path with its own state transitions and its own validation, in a panel whose entire value is that the environment is the only thing that moves the board.

Six registered probes, each executed through the same LabRunner path an ordinary experiment takes, so there is no shortcut by which a probe could report a result the engine did not produce. Reports which layer acted, because the distinction is the substance: the gate denied an attempt, the broker refused a request, or nothing was tested -- which is not a pass. No command can declare a breach or reclassify an outcome, and there is no combined security total.

Reconstructs recorded data and nothing else: no engine, no provider, no broker, so it cannot execute or authorize anything and cannot call a model by accident. An arena recording is re-executable; an experiment recording is an event stream and is labelled inspection-only, because the intermediate environment states were never captured. Limitations are rendered in full, since a replay that quietly filled a gap would be fabricating history.

Ranks two or more stored experiments, or refuses and names the dimensions that were not held constant. The refusal is a tagged response rather than an absence, so a panel has to handle it. Broker refusals and policy violations are counted separately and only the latter sets the security-finding flag. Provider, model, and benchmark definition digest BLOCK a comparison: a ranking may never span two subjects or two tasks. Absence is not difference, so a run that recorded no identity does not block on its own, and the deterministic mock is exempt from the model check because its model string is derived from its own strategy and is already a declared agent confound.

Defaults for future runs, stored in a backend SQLite file separate from the results database, so a settings reset is structurally incapable of reaching a measurement. Every write is validated in the core crate before it is persisted, and the response is the stored document rather than the submitted one, so a panel cannot display a value the backend adjusted or refused. There is no field anywhere in the document that could hold a credential.

Chat Completions over HTTPS or loopback, with redirects and retries disabled, credentials read from the environment by the adapter and never crossing the IPC boundary. The only provider the run configuration admits. Measured across the full episode pool through the multi-episode runner, not only the single-run path: run_experiment registers a connected agent for one run and the result carries an episode count, a Wilson interval, and a recorded provider, model, fingerprint, and task digest. Proven end to end against a local stand-in provider; no real vendor model has been measured. The transport reaches any server exposing /v1/chat/completions; that is a protocol statement, not a tested claim.

The Messages API adapter exists, is unit tested against the same transport rules, and joins multi-block content so a reply split across blocks is not misreported as unparseable. It is NOT selectable in the desktop product: `ConnectedProvider` has one variant. Its descriptor also omits configuration_fingerprint, prompt_template_version, and environment_version, so a run through it would record those three as empty -- see docs/STATUS.md 6.3. Partial rather than complete because the adapter is a library artifact, not a product capability.

The generateContent adapter exists and constrains the model name, because it goes into a URL path. NOT selectable in the desktop product. Same descriptor gap as the Anthropic adapter: an empty fingerprint, prompt version, and environment version. Partial rather than complete for the same reason.

Deliberately absent. The OpenAI-compatible transport already reaches a local Ollama server that exposes /v1, so a native adapter would be a second transport for the same protocol, maintained for branding rather than for a capability the product lacks.

Deliberately absent. OpenCode is a coding-agent tooling environment, not a model endpoint. Registering it as a provider would be a category error: a tool that calls models is not a thing that answers a chat-completions request.

The only authorization authority, depending on nothing but the core types -- it holds no model handle, so there is nothing for an agent to reach through. Deny by default, with canonicalized path checks, independent read and write roots, explicit program and endpoint allowlists with no defaults, and an unconditional environment.inspect denial that has no grant path. Traversal and symlink escape are refused. A denial is value-free, so a refusal can never become a probe for what was asked.

Windows only; every other platform fails closed with UnsupportedPlatform rather than running unconfined. A child starts suspended, inside a job object with CPU, memory, and process-count limits and KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, under a derived AppContainer package identity whose TokenAppContainerSid is read back and compared before resume, at low mandatory integrity, able to write only to a designated directory, with outbound network refused by the OS, an empty environment, a mandatory wall-clock timeout, and stdout/stderr redirected into the run's own directory. This is not a code sandbox: no syscall filtering, no filesystem or registry virtualization, no control over native code loading.

The measurement method: declared dev and eval seed pools validated as disjoint both when the definition loads and again in the constructor, N episodes over a pool, and a success rate with a Wilson interval. Wilson rather than the normal approximation because the approximation collapses to zero width. A run cut short by the wall-clock budget records its own terminal reason and its elapsed time, and the panel states that the score describes only the episodes that finished.

Nine hash-routed destinations in a persistent sidebar, with the active one marked by colour, a left bar, and aria-current rather than by colour alone. A real button list in a labelled landmark, with a skip link. No routing dependency. Registers no command of its own: it routes between the panels below, every one of which is driven by their commands, so `brain_panel` is named as the witness. No nav item leads nowhere, and the checker verifies that by comparing the frontend's real invoke calls against the real handler list.

Append-only telemetry with a gap-free per-run sequence, immutable results carrying an immutability trigger, a durable action trace, and lifecycle rows. Settings live in a separate file so a reset cannot reach a measurement. A row still saying running at start-up is provably wrong, so it is marked interrupted and logged rather than left to make a crashed run look complete. The running state is persisted BEFORE the first episode, which is what makes a mid-run crash detectable at all.

Field names, enum spellings, and absence semantics pinned against hand-written literals rather than asserted by round trip, because a round-trip test passes when both ends drift together. Every enum that reaches stored data or the IPC boundary has a wire_name derived from its serde definition and a test asserting the two agree, because four call sites were retyping the same enum four ways and one was storing a Debug rendering in a database column. serde_json's float_roundtrip is enabled so a stored f64 comes back bit-identical.

The frontend is untrusted input, so the boundary is tested with what a stale, buggy, or hostile build sends: malformed JSON, missing required fields, unknown fields, case-shifted field names, numbers given as strings, negative counts, unknown tags and strategies, schema-version drift, undeclared credential fields, base URLs with embedded credentials, and path-shaped identifiers. Every refusal is a typed refusal rather than a panic, an overflow, or a value reaching the engine unvalidated. A poisoned state lock returns an error instead of crashing the process.

cargo-deny over advisories, licences, duplicate versions, and allowed sources, checked in both the Linux and Windows CI jobs with a required clean exit rather than trusting the action's pass/fail. Fail-closed: unknown registries and unknown git sources are denied, unlicensed crates are denied, and licence confidence is 0.93 with no OSI-category shortcuts. Six documented advisory exceptions, all unmaintained notices reachable only through Tauri, each naming its path in.

A second, independent probe system of three prompt-injection and decoy-secret probes, wired into LabRunner and LabBrain. Library-reachable and product-unreachable: the desktop always sends an empty probe_agents list, so it never runs. Partial because it is a real capability with no product surface, and the security lab's six agent-registry probes are a different thing.

Verified discovery of all four execution modes: offline runtimes (Ollama, llama.cpp with GGUF listing, never downloaded; availability requires a 2xx JSON answer from GET /v1/models, not a TCP answer), installed coding agents (Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code with existence-only auth detection), guided external packages, and optional remote providers. Served model identifiers are enumerable per runtime for selection. Unavailable executors report the reason and remedy. Preflight runs only version checks and loopback connects. Guest-isolation support is inspectable read-only (OS, hypervisor, Sandbox/Hyper-V feature state) with a standing guided-only verdict.

Seed-varying coding-repair (8 bug patterns, hidden static checks, partial credit) and memory-latch (cue shown once, chance baseline 1/3) task benchmarks with 40 dev / 70 eval disjoint seed pools, Wilson intervals, definition digests, and reference ceilings/floors with disjoint intervals. Installed agents are measured through guided packages scored by the same hidden checks with provenance always recorded; automatic CLI-agent execution is refused at the product boundary because a workdir is not an isolation boundary.

Cooperative cancellation between episodes: the in-flight episode always finishes so cleanup runs, then the runner stops with a Cancelled terminal reason and a timeline entry. Handles are registered per experiment id and removed on completion, so a stale handle cannot stop a later run. A token-budget cap stops before the next episode with the same honesty.

Finished experiments export as pretty JSON (the full read model) or CSV (provenance header, per-episode rows, failures, aggregate with Wilson interval), read from the stored projection so the file cannot disagree with the panel. Unknown identifiers are refused rather than exported empty.
